chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in a bequest of his: 'Know that if the one who struck Ali (peace be upon him) with the sword and his killer were to entrust me and seek my good counsel and consult me, then if I had accepted that from him, I would have repaid the trust to him.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the killer of Imam Ali fulfilling a trust?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the supreme virtue of *amanah* (trustworthiness) by noting that even the killer of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) would receive his due trust if he sought it. This highlights the Shia concept of impartial justice, where the Imam’s fidelity to duties is not contingent on the recipient's merit or status, but on the integrity of the trust itself. It serves as a model for believers to maintain ethical consistency and fulfill obligations even towards adversaries.
